name: Invoices (/api/v1/invoices merchant API, /api/invoices UI)
description:
Creating an invoice never writes the invoices table here: the request is
  validated then published to the "invoices" queue, and payment_consumers
  creates the row - so every scenario that needs a row to actually exist
  (the real 202 QUEUED success path, and anything that reads or cancels a
  created invoice) is tagged @requires-rabbitmq and/or @requires-consumer and
  does not run by default in this environment (no broker is installed here).
  Everything else - validation, auth, not-found, listing/pagination - happens
  entirely inside payment_api and is exercised below without any broker.

name: Provider payment-response intake (/api/v1/payment-responses/{payerCode})
description:
Where M-Pesa, AstroPay and Airtel deliver payment results. Nothing is
  parsed, verified or decided here - the raw body and a few headers are
  published untouched to the payment_responses queue for payment_consumers'
  payer controllers to handle, so a provider gets a fast, uniform answer.
  There is deliberately no authentication (providers can't present a bearer
  token or API key), so success here only ever needs the payer code to
  resolve and the broker to confirm the publish - the 200 response itself
  needs @requires-rabbitmq in this broker-less environment; payer resolution
  and the not-found path need neither and run by default.
  (PAYMENT_RESPONSE_ALLOWED_IPS is empty by default in this environment, so
  the IP-allowlist 403 branch is never reached and is not exercised here.)

name: Payments (/api/v1/payments merchant API, /api/payments UI)
description:
Like invoices, a payment request is validated then published to the
  "payments" queue - payment_consumers creates the row, applies the
  service's invoice rules, and calls the payer; the eventual
  PENDING_ACKNOWLEDGEMENT state (and a real acknowledgement happy path) only
  arises once a provider has actually answered, which is beyond what this
  broker-less environment can exercise. Scenarios tagged @requires-rabbitmq
  and/or @requires-consumer need that stack and do not run by default here;
  everything else (validation, auth, not-found, listing) is broker-independent
  and runs below.

name: Bulk invoice and payment uploads (/api/*/invoices/upload, /api/*/payments/upload, /api/uploads*)
description:
Unlike a single invoice or payment, the upload batch row itself is written
  by payment_api synchronously - only the individual valid rows are handed to
  the background publisher, which needs RabbitMQ to actually reach QUEUED.
  So the POST response (totalRows/validRows/invalidRows/errors, and whether
  the batch starts PUBLISHING or FAILED) is fully deterministic without any
  broker, and is exercised below without tags. Anything that waits for a
  batch to finish publishing or to complete is tagged @requires-rabbitmq
  and/or @requires-consumer.

name: Staff users, roles and permissions (/api/users, /api/roles, /api/permissions)

  payer_reports.view) can never be granted to a staff account.
